newsitem.title: USA: AMD says Digital Equipment to use K6 chip.
newsitem.headline: AMD says Digital Equipment to use K6 chip.

text.p: Advanced Micro Devices Inc said Thursday that Digital Equipment Corp will use its K6 microprocessor -- a rival to Intel Corp's Pentium -- in an upcoming line of personal computers.
At its annual shareholder meeting in New York, the chairman of AMD also said other big PC makers are evaluating the K6.
"Digital is impressed with AMD's K6 technology and we do plan to use it in future products," said Digital spokesman Dan Kafferle.
Digital is the first top-ten PC maker to sign up as a customer for AMD's K6 microprocessor.

AMD introduced the K6 earlier this month. The chip mimics the way Intel's Pentium chips work. It cruches numbers slightly faster than Intel's top-of-the-line Pentium Pro chip, but costs at least 25 percent less.
AMD, which has seen declining revenues in recent quarters, is pinning its financial future on the K6.
Jerry Sander, AMD chairman, told investors Thursday that the chipmaker will announce more top-tier customers in coming weeks.
